summary: Enterprise search vendor evaluating Redwood for a RAG pipeline: ANN recall + cross-encoder rerank. Focused on indexing scale (target 100M+ docs), sub-100ms p95 user queries, and aggressive cost-per-query targets. Needs robust vector DB connectors (bulk upsert, metadata filters, hybrid BM25 fallback) and data residency controls.
notes: Company background: mid-stage search infra company with legal/finance customers; heavy compliance needs. internal infra: mix of postgres + S3 + some legacy Elastic clusters.
Key ask: plug Redwood as inference + re-rank layer and integrate with customer-managed vector DBs (they will not allow vendor-hosted indices in EU).
Scale targets: initial POC 10M docs, scaling plan to 100M+ docs (120M doc target), approx 800M embeddings after augmentation. Query volume expected 20k qps read peaks across global regions.
Latency / cost goals: user-facing 95th pct <= 120ms end-to-end; reranker (cross-encoder) budget <= 70ms; total cost target ≈ $0.0008-$0.0012 per query across recall+rerank when amortized.

Architecture preference: ANN recall in customer vector DB (pgvector or Weaviate or Pinecone), then send top-K (K=50) back to Redwood Dedicated for cross-encoder re-ranking. Also want built-in BM25 hybrid fallback when vector recall confidence < threshold.
Connector wishlist (explicit):
- Bulk upsert API with resumable jobs and per-batch retries (upsert 10M docs in batches; must support multi-threaded ingestion).
- Incremental CDC-friendly ingest: Kafka or S3-backed backfill support, last-updated tombstones, idempotent upserts.
- Filtered recall: ability to apply boolean metadata filters and range filters at ANN search time (tenant_id, doc_type, pii_flag).
- Hybrid search support (vector + BM25) or deterministic fallback to BM25 with namespace blending.
- Namespace / multi-tenant isolation and per-namespace replication for EU residency.
- Low-cost cold-start options: warm cache hints or ability to pin hot partitions to GPU hosts.
POC notes (timeline):
- 2026-01-12: kickoff call. CTO quote: "Need to show 3x improvement over existing reranker pipeline for MRR while reducing cost by 40%."
- 2026-01-20: Fireflies transcript ff_20260120_kickoff (linked). initial data sample shared (500k documents).
- 2026-02-05: Redwood delivered small-scale demo using Pinecone + Redwood hosted cross-encoder. Result: top-5 MRR improved from 0.42 -> 0.61; avg reranker latency 68ms (on Dedicated dev tier).
- 2026-02-18: Onsite POC: ingested 2M docs into pgvector staging via custom bulk loader. Observed ingest bottleneck: writer throughput ~8k docs/min -> needs parallelization or direct S3->vec import.
- 2026-02-25: Security review kickoff; Stonebridge security: must have SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS integration, and 7yr audit log retention (asked to confirm).
Technical constraints and preferences:
- Prefer open connectors first: pgvector + Weaviate, fallback to Pinecone for managed operator if ingestion SLA is tight.
- Want Postgres-hosted vector DB for transactional joins with metadata (important for ACL enforcement).
- Reranker model: cross-encoder (fine-tuned) hosted on Redwood Dedicated with GPU; requires model pinning/versioning and canary rollouts.

- Need routing policy: high-priority interactive queries -> Dedicated (low-latency), batch analytics -> Hosted to save cost. Ability to set per-route SLOs and automatic fallback when Dedicated capacity is saturated.
Integration requirements (details for engineering):
- Connector must return stable top-K ordering for given seed and include vector distance scores and per-item metadata in a single API response.
- Support for sparse + dense hybrid (sparse features or keyword signals added as metadata/scalar fields).
- Upsert idempotency and write-through TTL semantics for ephemeral test namespaces.
Commercial and procurement notes:
- Prefers 12-24 month committed Dedicated capacity with an annual true-up clause. Budget owners need predictable unit economics to justify commit.
- Procurement has concerns on vendor access to EU-resident indices; must support customer-side managed infra (private control plane preferred).
Open questions / blockers captured:
- Can Redwood connector support bulk ingest at 100k+ docs/min into pgvector or Weaviate?
- Does Dedicated routing support per-tenant cost accounting for multi-tenant clusters?
- Security: confirm HSM/KMS integration steps and SLA for audit log exports.
Next steps (from AE):
- 2026-03-05: engineering sync to scope connector work and time-to-ingest improvements (Liam + Redwood infra engs).
- 2026-03-12: plan to run a 10M doc quick load using parallelized S3->pgvector import; measure time and failure modes.
- Procurement: deliver draft SOW and privacy addendum (Maya to share before 2026-03-22).
